name: MonarchThemeToggle
title: ThemeToggle
wrapsNative: Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented); Menu with an inline Picker and .menuStyle(.button), drawn with MonarchButtonStyle (ghost)
summary: Light, dark or system appearance, bound to the MonarchSchemePreference that the app passes to .monarchTheme(scheme:).
whenToUse: On a settings screen (segmented) or in a toolbar or account menu (menu) to let people choose the app's appearance.
whenNotToUse: Not for contrast or accent choices; use a standard Picker bound to MonarchContrastPreference or the accent. Not needed when the app always follows the device.
api: init(selection: Binding<MonarchSchemePreference>, variant: MonarchThemeToggleVariant = .segmented, size: MonarchThemeToggleSize = .md, showsLabel: Bool = true, labels: MonarchThemeToggleLabels = MonarchThemeToggleLabels())
static func storageValue(for preference: MonarchSchemePreference) -> String
struct MonarchThemeToggleLabels { var title, light, dark, system: String? }

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen scheme: .light, .dark or .system. The app applies it with .monarchTheme(scheme:) and stores it.

options.name: variant
options.description: segmented shows three segments; menu shows one button that opens the three choices.

options.name: size
options.description: sm or md. Segmented: the regular or the large system control. Menu: the sm or md Monarch button.

options.name: showsLabel
options.description: menu only: whether the button shows the current choice's name beside its symbol. Without it the name is still spoken.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings Theme, Light, Dark and System.

states.name: light, dark, system
states.description: The selected segment, or the checked menu item and the symbol and name on the menu button (sun, moon, half-filled circle).

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) the system dims the segmented control; the menu button uses the disabled roles of the Monarch button style.

appearance: The segmented variant is the system segmented control, whose selected segment follows the system look in light, dark and increased contrast. The menu variant is a ghost Monarch button: default text colour on no fill, a subtle fill while pressed, and the system menu with a checkmark on the current choice.
platformNotes: The web toggle reads and writes the shared rook_theme cookie and applies the theme to the html element itself. On iOS there is no shared cookie: the toggle only changes its binding, and the app stores the choice (for example with @AppStorage) and applies it with .monarchTheme(scheme:). storageValue(for:) and preference(storageValue:) use the same light, dark and system values as the cookie. The web menu variant's side and align options have no meaning for a system menu, which the system places. Segments show names only, because a system segmented control shows either text or an image per segment.
accessibility: Both variants are standard Pickers, so VoiceOver reads the choices as items with the current one selected, and the menu's choices carry the system checkmark.
The menu button is named Theme (or labels.title) and its value is the current choice's name, also when showsLabel is false.
The choices are named in words; the symbols are not the only sign of the choice.
The menu button has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points; the segmented control keeps the system control height.
edgeCases: Long translated names are truncated by the system segmented control; use the menu variant when names are long.
preference(storageValue:) returns nil for a missing or unknown stored value, so the app chooses its own default.
The toggle can sit inside a view whose theme it changes; the change applies as soon as the binding changes.
